subject: Gold Skulltulas
text: There are one hundred Gold Skulltulas hidden throughout Hyrule in both time periods of the game in roughly equal portions.

evidence.quote:
Ocarina of Time continues that
tradition with one hundred Gold Skulltulas hidden throughout Hyrule.

Hidden in both time periods of the game in roughly equal portions, the Gold
Skulltulas are the symbols of a curse that affects a wealthy family in Kakariko
Village.

subject: House of Skulltula
text: Finding, destroying, and taking magic tokens from Gold Skulltulas frees members of the cursed family in Kakariko Village, and visiting the House of Skulltula rewards Link with a special item.

evidence.quote:
There are six members in the family total, and finding, destroying,
and taking the magic token from enough Gold Skulltulas will free one of the
family members from his curse.  Visiting the House of Skulltula at that point
will get Link some kind of special item, usually beneficial, sometimes
laughably useless.

subject: Hookshot
text: When Link first reaches adulthood, he must obtain the Hookshot before he can do anything else.

evidence.quote:
The game's beginning, and first three dungeons, are always the same, and when
you first reach adulthood, you MUST obtain the Hookshot before you can do
anything else.

subject: Biggoron Sword Trading Sidequest
text: Once Link has Epona, the Biggoron Sword sidequest can be completed at any time.

evidence.quote:
Once you have Epona, you can complete the Biggoron Sword
Sidequest at ANY time.

subject: Fire Temple
text: The Fire Temple and Ice Cavern can both be completed without the Fairy Bow from the Forest Temple.

evidence.quote:
The Fire Temple and Ice Cavern
can both be completed without the Fairy Bow from the Forest Temple, just as the
Ice Cavern and Forest Temple can be completed without the Megaton Hammer from
the Fire Temple, and the Fire Temple and Forest Temple can be completed without
the Iron Boots from the Ice Cavern.

subject: Water Temple
text: Completing the Ice Cavern and the Forest Temple allows progression to the Water Temple before finishing the Fire Temple.

evidence.quote:
And if you're done with the Ice Cavern and
the Forest Temple, then you can proceed to the Water Temple before finishing
the Fire Temple.

subject: Gerudo Fortress
text: The Gerudo Fortress can be completed at any time once the Forest Temple is finished and Link has both the Fairy Bow and Epona.

evidence.quote:
Additionally, once you finish the Forest Temple and have the
Fairy Bow, and once you have Epona, then the Gerudo Fortress CAN be completed
at ANY time (though this guide will wait until you HAVE to do it).

subject: Bottom of the Well
text: After completing the Forest Temple, Link can return to childhood at any time, making the Bottom of the Well available.

evidence.quote:
Also, once
you have completed the Forest Temple, you can return to your childhood at any
time, at which point The Bottom of the Well also becomes available.

subject: Big Poe Hunting Sidequest
text: The Big Poe hunting sidequest can be completed at any time after obtaining Epona and getting the Fairy Bow.

evidence.quote:
Lastly,
the Big Poe Hunting sidequest can be completed at any time after obtaining
Epona and getting the Fairy Bow.

subject: Shadow Temple
text: The Bottom of the Well mini-dungeon must be completed before the Shadow Temple can be completed.

evidence.quote:
Before the Shadow Temple can be
completed, however, then the Bottom of the Well Mini-Dungeon MUST be completed.

subject: Spirit Temple
object: Bottom of the Well and Gerudo Fortress
text: Both the Bottom of the Well and the Gerudo Fortress must be completed before the Spirit Temple can be attempted.

evidence.quote:
And before the Spirit Temple can even be attempted, BOTH the Bottom of the Well
and the Gerudo Fortress must be completed.

subject: Piece of Heart
text: There are thirty-six hidden Pieces of Heart around Hyrule, and gathering four Pieces of Heart rewards an additional Heart Container, amounting to nine of the game's twenty available Heart Containers from Pieces of Heart.

evidence.quote:
Ocarina also honors it's predecessors with the inclusion of thirty-six hidden
Pieces of Heart.  Each Piece of Heart represents one-quarter of a Heart
Container, and gathering four Pieces of Heart rewards the player with an
additional Heart Container.  With thirty-six total Pieces of Heart hidden
around Hyrule, that amounts to nine of the game's twenty available Heart
Containers from Pieces of Heart.
